  • Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United has strengthened the opinion that Xabi Alonso may not necessarily be the correct fit as Chelsea manager.
  • Not only has the Spaniard defended the multiple occasions that Chelsea have allowed opponents to have the majority of possession, he was seemingly dismissive to the suggestion from the media that his players lack the physicality to compete against the majority of the teams in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 12:25.

Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United has strengthened the opinion that Xabi Alonso may not necessarily be the correct fit as Chelsea manager.

Not only has the Spaniard defended the multiple occasions that Chelsea have allowed opponents to have the majority of possession, he was seemingly dismissive to the suggestion from the media that his players lack the physicality to compete against the majority of the teams in the Premier League.

Should Chelsea lose at Nottingham Forest - another team far more physically-imposing than themselves - on Friday night, Alonso's win percentage after 15 matches would be almost identical to that of Liam Rosenior's after 23 games.

While that creates an argument that Chelsea's players are to blame for their fall from grace rather than the Spaniard or Englishman, Alonso is responsible for a number of baffling decisions during his time at Stamford Bridge.

Here, Sports Mole highlights nine mistakes that Alonso has made since he was declared as the club's fresh manager in May.

With Valentin Barco announcing that he was leaving Strasbourg on May 19, the deal to take him to fellow BlueCo-owned club Chelsea could have been concluded before Alonso's appointment.

However, for unknown reasons, it was not announced until August 2, suggesting that there was time for Alonso to veto the transfer.

In a recent development, at 5ft 7ins and of slender build, Barco is simply not equipped to be a Premier League midfielder. While he may have starred for Strasbourg, the Argentine is not a suitable fit alongside Chelsea's other engine-room options.

He has reached this stage of the season with three starts and four substitute appearances, with just 25 minutes coming since October 10.

Given the amount of game time that Marco Palestra was given during pre-season, it was clear that Alonso viewed the Italian as a first-choice pick at full-back or wing-back.

Nevertheless, Alonso got carried away. Palestra racked up 311 minutes across four pre-season friendlies played between August 1 and August 15, and the former Atalanta BC player suffered an injury in the days before the opening Premier League game of the season against Fulham.

That prevented the Serie A defender of the year from making his debut until October 10, effectively having to play catch-up as he attempts to acclimatise to English football.

While the 21-year-old started the recent win over Manchester United, he is yet to convince in his current role.

After an extended season that saw him represent Ecuador at the World Cup on July 1, Moises Caicedo was back playing friendlies for Chelsea in the Middle East by August 5.

The midfielder subsequently started three friendlies across 10 days and, like Palestra, suffered an injury in the build-up to the Fulham game.

Caicedo then lasted just 14 minutes on his return from the substitutes' bench against Brighton & Hove Albion six days later and was not seen again until October 10.

He has suffered with a lingering issue ever since, and the way in which Alonso used players during pre-season deserves more scrutiny than it has done.

Alonso went from naming a stronger team than anticipated against Luton Town in the EFL Cup second round to making many alterations versus Leeds United in round three.

Some of that decision-making was justified, yet Alonso himself has taken responsibility for making what he states were too many changes for the latter match.

Chelsea ultimately came from 2-0 down to prevail by a 6-3 scoreline in a crazy game, but withdrawing Estevao Willian after 45 minutes started the ball rolling when it came to the Brazilian's frustration over his game time.

Not only did Jordan Henderson make his first start since the World Cup, with no pre-season, in this match, Alonso partnered the veteran Englishman with Barco, who was making his first Premier League start for Chelsea.

Although Chelsea held Brentford for the first hour and Henderson produced a solid performance on debut, this game exposed that Barco weakens Chelsea's midfield, rather than add any match-winning qualities.

Romeo Lavia also remained an unused substitute in this contest, one which Chelsea lost by a 3-0 scoreline.

While some Chelsea fans had been waiting for Geovany Quenda to be handed his first start for Chelsea, they did not anticipate it coming in a London derby against Tottenham Hotspur.

Furthermore, his selection led to Morgan Rogers taking on the number nine role, rather than Danny Welbeck, in the absence of the injured Joao Pedro.

Industry observers note that chelsea subsequently produced one of their most ineffective performances in the final third this season. That was not necessarily because of Quenda, but more through a lack of a traditional number nine to trouble the Spurs defence.

Two weeks later, Alonso chose the same approach against Sunderland, this time using Pedro Neto down the middle.

This decision was essentially made because Chelsea beat Manchester United in the previous game, yet the Red Devils had been the better team in the first half at Stamford Bridge without scoring their opener.

Although there is an argument that Welbeck has not made the expected impact at Chelsea, the 35-year-old has not been given a chance to build up any rhythm and is immediately benched on the back of an ineffective performance.

Despite Emiliano Martinez being signed from Aston Villa to be Chelsea's number one, the Argentine had hardly been at his best prior to suffering a fractured jaw at Everton on October 17.

Meanwhile, Mike Penders recovered from a mistake on his first Premier League start against Spurs to deliver strong showings versus Liverpool, Manchester United and Sunderland, with the only two goals that he conceded coming from penalties.

Regardless, Martinez was back in the starting lineup against Leeds on Saturday, the 34-year-old conceding four goals and making Chelsea appear more vulnerable in defence than they already were.

Alonso has previously indicated that players will be selected on form, but this was a glaring example of choosing status over performances.

It has been revealed that martinez has now conceded 15 goals in 615 minutes for Chelsea. Penders has shipped seven goals in 555 minutes.

Estevao had already struggled against Leeds earlier this season, so the starlet being drafted back into the Chelsea XI for a second Stamford Bridge game versus the Yorkshire giants felt strange.

Furthermore, his inclusion was ahead of Neto, who is Chelsea's strongest winger when it comes to strength and defending. Alonso has already recognised this by using the Portuguese as a wing-back this season.

Recent findings suggest that neto being omitted from the first XI for a game against opponents of the profile of Leeds made no sense and was more muddled thinking from Alonso. Chelsea were already 3-1 down before he was introduced as a substitute.

#174912. The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1178 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1178 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • In a recent development, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

In a recent development, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

The plate and the photos are on show at the new exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, notes exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Sources indicate that alongside Picasso, a surprising number of vital artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to glitch a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Recent findings suggest that still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

However, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

Industry observers note that the dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked significant and dangerous.".

Sources indicate that the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian says. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a newly introduced image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

It has been revealed that the designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

According to recent reports, still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

According to recent reports, but altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 12:42.

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury patch on Manchester City’s Matheus Nunes ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

The 28-year-old was unable to recover in time from an ankle problem to feature in City’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham on Saturday.

Nunes has been absent for four of the Citizens’ last seven games in all tournaments this term, but Maresca confirmed at a pre-match press conference on Monday that the right-back “is back” and ready to face Napoli.

In a recent development, "Matheus is back. Then the only one [out] is still Antoine [Semenyo],” Maresca told reporters. “The rest, we have some doubts in terms of tiredness, amount of games, and we have today's session and then we'll decide.".

In a recent development, pushed for more details on Nunes’s recent injury, Maresca added: "This one has been a little bit his ankle, but now he's fine. It's also normal with the amount of games we have, that's why also sometimes I try to rotate players.

Industry observers note that "I've stated many times, we need to not think about a sprint, we need to think about a marathon; 65 games. So I would like to use the strongest one every game, but then we destroy them. It's also a matter of trying to manage them the best way.”.

Nunes has established himself as Man City’s first-choice right-back when fit and available, while Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis have also been used on the right side of defence under Maresca and predecessor Pep Guardiola.

Man City’s No.27 has played 10 times across all competitions so far this season, but he has been left out of the matchday squad for five games due to injury or fitness-related complications.

According to recent reports, "Since we started, we've used Rico [Lewis at right-back], but also [Khusanov], who I think he can play there,” Maresca explained. “For sure, it's much better... I'm trying to find the right balance.

"If you ask me if Khusa is a better right-back or central defender, no doubt: Central defender. I know that. But it's a matter of the game, the players we have available.

Recent findings suggest that "But Matheus [Nunes] has done very good since we started, the games he has played, overall he was very good. Rico has [also] done very good so far.”.

It remains to be seen whether Maresca will throw Nunes straight back into the starting lineup against Napoli, with one eye possibly on Sunday’s notable Premier League showdown with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Man City have won three of their first four Champions League games in the League Phase and can strengthen their automatic last-16 qualification hopes with a victory against Napoli, who have lost three of their opening four matches in the competition.

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 12:44.

Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee could reportedly become the first player to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

The Dutchman joined the Red Devils from Bologna in the summer of 2024 and has since made 86 appearances for the club across all competitions.

Zirkzee has managed just 11 goals and four assists for Man Utd and was heavily linked with a move away from the club during the summer transfer window.

Several Serie A clubs were keen to sign him, with Fiorentina reportedly agreeing a loan fee for the striker, but the proposed move ultimately failed to materialise.

Premier League rivals Everton also made a late push for the 25-year-old, but Man Utd were unwilling to let him leave without first securing a replacement.

Former Man Utd manager Michael Carrick even suggested that Zirkzee could become an crucial player for the club, but the striker has since slipped considerably down the pecking order.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (via Manchester Evening News), Zirkzee is expected to become the first player to depart in January, with several Italian clubs competing for his signature.

Juventus and Fiorentina are reportedly keen to sign the striker, while Napoli could also enter the race.

The former Bayern Munich attacker has made just seven substitute appearances in the Premier League this season, accumulating 134 minutes of action and scoring once.

Zirkzee has also featured three times as a substitute in the Champions League, where he has registered another goal.

Mauricio Pochettino introduced him in the second half of Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, and the Dutchman managed to make a positive impression despite the disappointing result.

Towards the end of the contest, Zirkzee produced a brilliant pass to Bruno Fernandes, but the United captain's effort was comfortably saved by Alisson Becker.

If Zirkzee fails to earn more opportunities under Pochettino over the coming month, the likelihood of him leaving Old Trafford could increase considerably.

Real Madrid: Mourinho faces attacking dilemma ahead of Champions League clash with PSV

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19.
  • Industry observers note that real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with important issues for Jose Mourinho to manage.
  • Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19.

Industry observers note that real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with important issues for Jose Mourinho to manage. Saturday's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo was another example of the team's ability to react, but it also exposed problems that the manager cannot ignore.

Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match. The Brazilian, who had served a four-match suspension in La Liga, has regained prominence and has already had his place in the starting line-up for the European tie confirmed by Mourinho. At the same time, the Spanish centre-forward again highlighted that he can be decisive even with few minutes on the pitch.

The challenge is to find room for so many options without compromising the collective structure. Real Madrid have Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius, Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler, Yan Diomande and Espi, as well as names who could come into the mix, such as Endrick and Bernardo Silva, but they cannot simply put them all on the pitch and hope that individual talent solves everything.

Vinicius's display against Celta was a reminder of what the Brazilian offers Real Madrid. Coming on 12 minutes into the second half, he gave the attack depth and was able to unbalance defenders in one-on-one situations. For the equaliser, he started the move that ended with Bellingham. For the winner, he crossed for Espi to pounce on the rebound.

Mourinho confirmed that the Brazilian will start against PSV, ending the debate about his status in the team. Peter Bosz's side are known for high pressing, aggressive defending and their attempts to win the ball back swiftly. When that first press is beaten, however, they tend to offer space behind the defenders.

In a recent development, that is precisely where Vinicius can be decisive. With his acceleration and ability to attack the space in behind, the Brazilian is a constant threat to a defence that often plays a high line and takes on individual duels all over the pitch. Mbappe can also exploit these spaces.

The question for Mourinho is how to make this threat work without leaving the midfield exposed. Real Madrid cannot rely solely on winning the ball back and launching it to the forwards. They need players close by to connect transitions and sustain possession when necessary.

The presence of Bellingham and Guler between the lines could be important. The Englishman offers ball-carrying and arrivals into the box, while the Turkey international has the quality to find passes that speed up the attack. But the team needs a solid base behind them. Without that, the freedom of the attacking players could prove costly.

In a recent development, espi's situation is another dilemma. The 21-year-old forward scored the winner against Celta and has three goals in only 44 minutes played in La Liga this season. It is impressive efficiency, but it does not necessarily mean that he should start.

Mourinho was clear in explaining the Spaniard's characteristics. Espi is a penalty-box centre-forward, strong in the air, able to play with his back to goal and to attack the spaces close to the six-yard box. He is not, however, a forward with great mobility to take part constantly in build-up play. The manager also remarked that the squad does not have the right characteristics to play a pure 4-4-2 with Mbappe and Espi together.

According to recent reports, mbappe likes to start from the left or occupy the space between the full-back and the centre-back, but he is not a traditional winger who tracks the opposition full-back back into his own half. Vinicius also needs freedom to receive the ball wide and accelerate. Putting Espi alongside the Frenchman would require the two wide players to tuck in more and help form a four-man midfield line.

There are alternatives, but all involve compromises. Bellingham could play deeper, for example. The problem is that Real Madrid would lose part of the Englishman's ability to arrive in the box and would need a midfielder with greater defensive responsibility to compensate. It would also be possible to use Espi in matches where the opposition sit deep and offer less space for the runs of Vinicius and Mbappe.

Sources indicate that against tired defences and crosses, Espi offers something different from the other forwards in the squad. His efficiency as a substitute should not be confused with an obligation to change the whole structure of the team.

Recent findings suggest that the win over Celta also left a warning. After turning the scoreline around, Real Madrid finished the game with four forwards on the pitch, as well as Bellingham and Guler in midfield. Mourinho admitted that the team became unbalanced and that he would have liked an extra substitution to bring on Tchouameni and restore defensive protection.

Under Bosz, PSV rely on high pressing, dominating possession, constant movement and a defence that often takes on individual duels. The full-backs can advance into midfield and the forwards take part in the press. It is an aggressive model, capable of suffocating opponents, but one that also leaves space when the first line is beaten.

The impact of each at Real Madrid in 2026-27.

Recent findings suggest that direct involvements = goals + assists. In the Champions League, Vinicius played four games without a goal or an assist; Espi scored one goal in four games, against Roma. Points gained assume that, without Espi's goals, the three games would have ended in draws. Data up to 21 November 2026.

Sources: FotMob (Opta data), AS and TheStatsAPI.

Real Madrid have the tools to exploit these gaps. Vinicius and Mbappe can attack the space in behind, while Bellingham and Guler have the ability to receive between the lines and speed up the transition. The difficulty will be doing so without turning the game into a series of attacks and counter-attacks.

Sources indicate that real Madrid won their first four league-phase games in the Champions League and are second, with 12 points. The positive run brings calm, but it does not remove the need to improve the collective performance.

Mourinho already has an answer to one of the questions: Vinicius will start. He also knows what Espi can offer and why he does not intend simply to put him alongside Mbappe. The bigger challenge is to make Real Madrid take advantage of the quality of their attackers without losing control of midfield.

#174902. Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

📅 23 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1045 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1045 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.
  • According to recent reports, "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW.
  • The jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

According to recent reports, "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it.".

The jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

Industry observers note that "A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity.".

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

Industry observers note that but a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, shows how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

Names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer mentioned their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages.".

In a recent development, research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

"Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

In a recent development, even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on.".

In a recent development, pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

"People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'".

Later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she mentioned.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

Tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to.".

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions.".

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'".

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point.".

It has been revealed that but the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

"I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there.".

But Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum mentioned.

Tiny describes a similar ambivalence.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it.".

Sources indicate that that does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

Online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered.".

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

Pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny.".

  • Barcelona will aim to make it five straight wins in all competitions when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sabah on Wednesday night.
  • History will be made in this contest, as the two teams prepare to lock horns for the first time, and it would be one of the biggest shocks in Champions League history should Sabah manage to overcome the La Liga champions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 13:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Barcelona will aim to make it five straight wins in all competitions when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sabah on Wednesday night.

History will be made in this contest, as the two teams prepare to lock horns for the first time, and it would be one of the biggest shocks in Champions League history should Sabah manage to overcome the La Liga champions.

Sabah boast a record of one win and three draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League league phase, which has left them in 31st spot in the table on three points, one point behind 24th-placed PSV Eindhoven.

The Owls opened their league stage campaign with a 4-0 loss to Manchester United, before managing to record a 2-0 victory over Slavia Prague in their second fixture to put three points on the board, but they have since lost to Borussia Dortmund and Viking FC.

Valdas Dambrauskas's side will enter this match off the back of a huge domestic win, beating Sumqayit 5-1, with the result leaving them third in Azerbaijan's top flight, picking up 24 points from their opening 11 games of the season.

Including qualification matches, Sabah have a record of seven wins and five losses in this season's Champions League, keeping five clean sheets in the process.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, so it is a historic campaign for the club, and they will take on Villarreal, Napoli and Arsenal in their three Champions League league stage fixtures after this one.

As for Barcelona, the Catalan side are currently fifth in the league phase table, picking up nine points from their four matches courtesy of a record of three wins and one defeat.

Hansi Flick's side beat Feyenoord and Galatasaray in their opening two league stage fixtures before suffering a 4-2 reverse to Paris Saint-Germain, but they managed to post a 3-0 victory over Aston Villa last time out to get back on track.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Villarreal, with that result moving them back to the top of the La Liga table, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

The Catalan side lost in the last-16 stage of last season's Champions League to Atletico Madrid, and it remains to be seen whether their defensive unit is strong enough to make a serious challenge for the 2026-27 European Cup.

Barcelona have actually conceded in each of their last 12 away group stage/league phase matches, but they have scored at least twice in 17 of their last 19 games at this point.

Barcelona Champions League form:.

Barcelona form (all competitions):.

Sabah will be without the services of Aden McCarthy, with the centre-back suspended on Wednesday following his red card in the team's last Champions League match with Viking.

The hosts also need to make a check on the fitness of Veljko Simic, who is struggling with an injury; the attacker has eight goals in 18 appearances this season and his absence would therefore be a major blow for Sabah.

Joy-Lance Mickels has been in impressive form this season, scoring 12 goals in 22 appearances, and the forward is set to start for the home team.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal will not be involved due to a slight ankle problem, with Barcelona not prepared to take any risks when it comes to the Spain international.

Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle), Rodri (hamstring) and Andreas Christensen (muscle) are also unavailable for selection.

Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal on Sunday due to an issue that he sustained while on international duty with Spain, but the centre-back was on the bench and should feature in the starting team.

Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi are expected to join Raphinha in the final third of the field due to the absence of Yamal.

Sabah possible starting lineup:.

Pokatilov; Zedadka, Solvet, Almeida, Puchaz; Lepinjica, Isayev, Rakhomaliev; Severina, Mbina, Mickels.

Barcelona possible starting lineup:.

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Adeyemi, Raphinha, Gordon.

Yamal's absence is a major blow for Barcelona, but the Catalan outfit have enough quality in their side to secure all three points on Wednesday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.
  • This was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce.
  • In a recent development, the atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

This was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

In a recent development, the atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

This was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

According to recent reports, “I have to take the responsibility,” he stated. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the plan. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

Recent findings suggest that “As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the plan disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it shows.”.

Newcastle looked listless, clueless and alarmingly devoid of belief in what they were being asked to do. They have the unmistakable whiff of a team in decline.

If they do not start playing a lot better, they will be worried about a relegation battle. It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

It has been revealed that concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight new signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat quickly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

In a recent development, there was no fluency and no threat. The first groans were heard inside 15 minutes as another pass was hoisted harmlessly into the air. They grew more widespread and more frequent.

Everton, just as they had in their Carabao Cup win last week, looked comfortable. Recognising how easy it was to nullify Newcastle’s game plan, they offered an attacking threat of their own.

Industry observers note that A rising shot from Merlin Röhl briefly had goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek worried. A free-kick into the Newcastle box caused panic. James Tarkowski won the first header, but Thierno Barry swung and missed with his left foot.

The groans began to turn into boos and whistles. Jaissle’s side could barely string more than two passes together. It felt precarious.

In a recent development, this is not an easy place to play football when the crowd airs its displeasure. As the first half limped on, there were players in black and white who looked like they could not handle the pressure.

In a recent development, it was a horrible game of football. With the last kick of the half, Everton should have taken the lead, Harrison Armstrong picked out Barry inside the box, but he made a mess of the finish. The referee’s whistle was accompanied by boos and a scream of “sort it out” from behind Jaissle’s technical area.

Industry observers note that he did not follow those blunt instructions. Newcastle appealed for both a foul on Fabian Schar and an offside but got neither.

Microbiome home tests are taking off. Can they be trusted?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A mix of microorganisms from a human faecal sample, imaged using a scanning electron microscope.
  • First, the good news: I have 133 microbial species living in my gut.
  • Revealed: how this common gut microbe protects against heart disease.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A mix of microorganisms from a human faecal sample, imaged using a scanning electron microscope. Credit: Steve Gschmeissner/Science Photo Library.

First, the good news: I have 133 microbial species living in my gut. That’s a collection that ranks as ‘excellent’ according to NirvanaBiome, the company in Germantown, Maryland, that analysed my stool sample. The firm based its rating on the overall diversity of my gut’s residents plus my levels of specific beneficial and undesirable species.

Revealed: how this common gut microbe protects against heart disease.

Revealed: how this common gut microbe protects against heart disease.

Industry observers note that but then came a second, less promising assessment: Viome in Bellevue, Washington, identified only 61 kinds of active microorganism in my gut and suggested that some of them were not performing optimally. Viome recommended dietary changes and offered customized supplements to improve my health.

In a recent development, I was intrigued by the results, but also flummoxed by the different messages. That’s not an uncommon response, says microbiologist Rob Knight, director of the Center for Microbiome Innovation at the University of California, San Diego. When scientists tested a handful of microbiome testing kits alongside one another in formal studies, they found wide discrepancies in the results. These differences make it hard to understand or really trust the findings from any given provider, says Diane Hoffmann, director of the Law and Health Care programme at the University of Maryland in Baltimore, who co-authored one of those studies.

Sources indicate that the companies stand by their products. “Of course there’s variability,” notes Kelly Moffat, chief operations officer for Cmbio in Germantown, which does the laboratory work and genetic sequencing for NirvanaBiome. “There has to be because this is complex testing.”.

It has been revealed that momo Vuyisich, chief science officer at Viome’s lab in Bothwell, Washington, also notes he was unsurprised by the degree of variation found by formal studies. Labs use different methods to extract, sequence and analyse microbial genetic material. Viome, for example, sequences RNA rather than DNA, allowing it to uncover microbial gene activity, rather than only the presence of genes. Vuyisich argues that this is more relevant to human health. And he says that although every method will have biases, as long as a consumer sticks with the same provider, it should produce results that are comparable over time.

Sources indicate that interest in these kinds of test is booming. “There’s so much public enthusiasm and excitement about the microbiome,” notes Knight. Some customers are simply curious about the microscopic beings that live inside them and potentially affect their health; others have health conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome and hope that their gut microbes will reveal the underlying cause or a path to better health.

According to recent reports, although people can order the tests and follow their recommendations without the help of a medical professional, some people are bringing the findings to their physicians. “I groan when I see someone come in with a microbiome test,” claims Fergus Shanahan, a gastroenterologist and immunologist at University College Cork in Ireland, who has spent much of his career studying the microbiome. For someone struggling with gut health, a consumer microbiome profile isn’t usually specific enough to help. And if there’s a concern about an infection, such as Clostridioides difficile, it’s more straightforward to test for known pathogens than to assess the entire microbial community.

The tantalizing links between gut microbes and the brain.

The tantalizing links between gut microbes and the brain.

According to recent reports, microbiologists and gasteroenterologists who spoke to Nature generally agreed that microbiome testing has the potential to both reflect and promote health, but many remarked that the science isn’t yet mature enough to support microbiome testing for most consumers. In their view, the limited clinical usefulness of today’s consumer tests can make them poor value for money (costing around US$100–300). The specialists warn that acting on advice that doesn’t come from clinicians could lead customers to adopt unnecessarily restrictive diets or delay appropriate medical assessment. Critics say that consumer microbiome testing needs more regulatory scrutiny and oversight.

In a recent development, “This is an industry that’s running wild,” says genomicist Jacques Ravel, director of the Center for Advanced Microbiome Research and Innovation at the University of Maryland School of Medicine in Baltimore and a co-author on one of the studies that tested several providers. With regards to testing methods, he says, “there’s no standard”.

Moffat claims, “I think the jury’s out on exactly what it is that we can actionably do today based on this data.” But she says that microbiome profiles, combined with other testing such as gut metabolomics, could yield interesting and useful health information.

The gut microbiome has emerged as an incredible correlate of overall health. From immune-system function to metabolism, skin disorders and mental health, study after study has found links between a person’s well-being and the trillions of microbes that live in their digestive tract. The premise of a head count of these species and assessment of their actions, to monitor and improve gut health in a personalized way, certainly sounds appealing. Viome’s website, for example, promises: “No more trial and error … Follow a plan built precisely for you.”.

Sources indicate that companies can identify species and, on the basis of those lists, infer what the microbes are probably doing, such as manufacturing metabolites or inciting inflammation. But running even the simplest microbiome testing is expensive, indicates Alessandra Cervino, research director at PiLeJe, a science-based food-supplement organization in Paris. She says her microbiome testing company, Luxia Scientific, closed in 2024 for financial reasons.

Some microbiome testing firms recommend fermented foods, such as kombucha, for gut health.Credit: Deb Lindsey for The Washington Post via Getty.

Sources indicate that many testing companies also offer lifestyle and nutritional advice or sell supplements. For example, Viome analysed diverse functions performed by the microbes in my gut, such as digestive efficiency, gas production and serotonin manufacture. I then received a detailed eating proposal — which told me to eschew broccoli and load up on pecans, among other suggestions — along with an offer for precision supplements and probiotics with a price tag of more than $150 a month. Although it’s hard to change the composition of microbes in one’s gut, alterations in diet or even simply ageing can shift their activities, says Vuyisich. The company recommends re-testing every four to six months to check for shifts and update the plan.

In a recent development, he points to 19 peer-reviewed publications by Viome as evidence of the tech giant’s rigour (see go.nature.com/4actdhq). For example, the firm’s analysis for consumers is supported, in part, by published data on how gut microbes influence individuals’ responses to glucose in various foods, based on 550 people in the United States who collectively ate more than 30,000 meals while wearing glucose monitors1. The company validated those findings in a further cohort in Japan, Vuyisich states, but those data are not published.

Microbiome tests are not created equal, states Tim Spector, a physician-scientist at King’s College London and co-founder of London-based ZOE, which offers microbiome testing and a supplement in addition to a gut-health app that I’ve been playing with. ZOE’s products, Spector says, are backed by research on thousands of people. “There definitely are some not-so-good players out there that give this field a bad name,” he says. “It’s not easy to do this well.”.

According to recent reports, there are also several ways to do microbe testing; companies take varying approaches that yield disparate results, as at least two studies have shown. Scientists at the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Gaithersburg, Maryland, shipped homogenized stool samples from one person to seven companies2. NIST’s remit is researching and applying standards for measurement. This experiment was a step towards understanding the diversity of testing options out there, says one of the study authors, NIST microbiologist Stephanie Servetas, who is based in Sheridan, Wyoming. The researchers didn’t name the companies in their report because they wanted to focus attention on the comparison between tests rather than perceived accuracy of any individual provider.

Industry observers note that the result: “Companies produce strikingly different results,” claims co-author Scott Jackson, a molecular geneticist who used to direct the NIST microbiology program and is now a consultant in Saint Michaels, Maryland. “They couldn’t even agree on what’s healthy and unhealthy,” Jackson says. The microbe lists ranged from 34 to 906 identified genera; only 3 of which revealed up in all reports. In fact, the results were as varied from company to company as they would be for different people, despite all tests being done on samples from the same individual.

According to recent reports, A European and Canadian team obtained similar outcomes when they sent homogenized samples from one person’s stool to six companies, also anonymized. Three companies rated the microbial diversity as “excellent” or “good”; two called it “average”; one mentioned it was “unfavourable”3. The results were so variable, that at least some of them must be lacking in validation or standardization, claims co-author Céline Druart, executive director of the Pharmabiotic Research Institute (PRI) in Brussels, a non-profit organization specializing in regulation of microbiome innovations. “It’s very difficult to make a conclusion,” she says.

How gut bacteria could boost cancer treatments.

How gut bacteria could boost cancer treatments.

Industry observers note that this broad divergence in results is not surprising, says Jack Gilbert, director of the Microbiome and Metagenomics Center at the University of California, San Diego. The variation starts at sampling: scoop a bit of faecal matter into a tube, stab it with a coring device or swipe the sampler across some used toilet paper; ship it off as-is, or in some kind of preservative (as both Viome’s and NirvanaBiome’s kits asked me to). Each option could influence the balance of the microbes that are collected and what survives to be sequenced.

In the lab, Servetas says the method by which the researchers extract genetic material from a sample is a significant source of divergence. Gentler protocols will bias a sample towards microbes that are easy to crack open, whereas harsher methods will capture a higher share of species with tougher exteriors.

After sequencing, another major source of difference, states Knight, is the bioinformatics pipeline that labs use. What length or number of genetic sequences is required to consider a microbe present? What list of sequences and microbes are they using as a reference? “All bets are off when you then computationally analyse it with your favourite method,” says Knight.

Would companies support having standards to validate their tests? “We are really major advocates on really having a standard here,” says Kimberley Sukhum, chief science officer at Tiny Health in Austin, Texas, which offers gut microbiome tests as well as vaginal microbiome tests.

Recent findings suggest that but it’s hard to set those standards, in part because there is no known ‘ground truth’ for a natural microbial sample. Compare that with, say, a blood-glucose test; a lab can get a known value from a standard sample either right or wrong. But the microbiome, in its glorious complexity, does not allow for such simple validation. NIST has used mixed human donor samples to develop a standard4. And Tiny Health has experimented with generating a reference for benchmarking from synthetic communities. It was built from individual microbial species rather than sampled from faeces5. But neither of those standards is exactly like the microbiome of an individual person.

Even if labs could assess a microbiome perfectly, they’d still have a problem: there’s no defined healthy microbiome like there is one range of healthy blood-glucose levels. Each person’s microbiome is unique, like a fingerprint. There are infinitely many ways to have a healthy microbiome, and infinitely many ways to have an unhealthy one, states Shanahan; it’s not entirely clear how to draw a line between the two.

How gut microbes could drive brain disorders.

How gut microbes could drive brain disorders.

Companies must compare customer microbiomes with some standard of health, but these vary too. They might be based on past customers or large, public databases. But microbiomes differ considerably depending on factors such as ethnicity, sex, age, recent antibiotic use or even whether someone was born by caesarean section.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32.

Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.

Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.

The England international has gradually slipped down the pecking order at the Santiago Bernabeu under Jose Mourinho, with Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries seemingly ahead of him.

Alexander-Arnold was also subjected to boos from sections of the home support following his lacklustre performance in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo last week.

Former Liverpool and England striker Emile Heskey recently suggested that Alexander-Arnold should consider a move to Bayern, although he admitted he would love to see the defender return to Anfield.

However, Bild journalist Christian Falk has categorically dismissed the links, suggesting that Bayern are more interested in signing players such as Givairo Read than Alexander-Arnold.

Bayern already have Konrad Laimer and Josip Stanisic available for the right-back position, while Sacha Boey also remains at the club.

Even if Vincent Kompany decides to make changes in that department, he would reportedly favour a younger profile, meaning Alexander-Arnold is unlikely to be a genuine option for the German champions.

Speaking to CFBayern Insider, Falk noted: "It is not true - Bayern Munich are interested in Real Madrid fullback Trent Alexander-Arnold. Bayern are searching for a player in this position, and players like Givairo Read are definitely still of interest.

Industry observers note that "You can tell from Read’s profile alone that the club just isn’t looking to add a player like Alexander-Arnold to the ranks. Also, I’m not sure if Vincent Kompany would look at the Englishman’s profile, as he’s not a typical right-back for Bayern Munich.

"He’s also not the youngest footballer any more. And, if we’re being honest, the 28-year-old hasn’t proven himself at Real Madrid.

"You have to have a lot of respect for English players who give it a go playing in another country. But not every English player succeeds after leaving the UK, and not every English player is Harry Kane! So, I don’t think Alexander-Arnold will be a genuine option for Bayern in the summer.".

While an emotional return to Anfield would appeal to many supporters, the reality is that Liverpool have probably moved on, even though the right-back position remains a somewhat problematic area for them.

Jeremie Frimpong has yet to convince everyone, while there is also uncertainty over whether the Reds will sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a permanent deal.

With Conor Bradley's injury record remaining a concern and Joe Gomez potentially departing next summer, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in a latest right-back, although it remains doubtful whether Liverpool would consider a move for their former player.

LA communities kick out Major Oil

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1063 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Los Angeles has become the largest city in the US to ban oil drilling, after years of lawsuits and campaigning by residents who raised the alarm over pollution and potential health risks from nearby wells .
  • "Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," said local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.
  • Industry observers note that the ordinance, approved by the LA City Council on October 28, puts an immediate stop to oil extraction and bans the redrilling or deepening of wells.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Los Angeles has become the largest city in the US to ban oil drilling, after years of lawsuits and campaigning by residents who raised the alarm over pollution and potential health risks from nearby wells .

"Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," said local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

Industry observers note that the ordinance, approved by the LA City Council on October 28, puts an immediate stop to oil extraction and bans the redrilling or deepening of wells. Existing operations must be phased out within city limits over the next 20 years.

Though LA City is only part of greater Los Angeles, the move affects hundreds of active wells and thousands of inactive ones, many located in working class communities of color.

It has been revealed that "In South LA, working-class families have had corporations drilling across the street from their homes," mentioned council president Marqueece Harris-Dawson in a statement. "No one should have to live near an oil drilling site.".

Rock Zierman, CEO of the California Independent Petroleum Association (CIPA), told DW, "CIPA believes this ordinance constitutes an unlawful taking of private property.".

LA follows much smaller Culver City, also in California, in moving against urban oil production, and begins the process of ending its long, complex relationship with fossil fuels.

California's oil industry expanded rapidly in the early 20th century, when the state produced roughly a quarter of the world's oil. Lots of that so-called black gold was around LA and as the city grew, homes, schools and businesses were built around existing oil infrastructure.

Today, wells can be found beneath residential areas, close to playgrounds, along the coast and in some of the city's most densely populated and largely working-class neighborhoods. Some have been permanently sealed or plugged for decades, while others remain active or are idle.

Under California law, an idle well is one that has not produced oil for two years. Unlike plugged wells, they can potentially return to production.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that residents living near the active and inactive wells report strong odors, headaches, nausea and breathing difficulties. Another concern is air quality. Oil wells can release toxic pollutants, including benzene and hydrogen sulfide, and research has linked proximity to oil extraction with higher rates of respiratory illness and reduced lung function.

But both active and idle wells can also leak methane — a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change — while residents say occasional accidents or breakages send oil flowing down city streets.

"Frontline communities have been experiencing or have experienced for decades living near these toxic sites and having to pay for that with their health," said Miranda, a policy director with Esperanza Community Housing, a nonprofit providing affordable housing services.

Sources indicate that miranda told DW she and her mother both have asthma. The council vote "definitely represents hope," she added.

LA City Council initially approved an ordinance to phase out oil extraction back in 2022 after successful lobbying by residents like Wendy Miranda. But oil companies challenged the measure in court, with industry groups successfully arguing that the city lacked the legal authority to impose the ban.

California subsequently passed legislation giving local governments greater power to regulate and restrict oil and gas operations, putting the possibility of a phaseout back on the table.

In an emailed statement to DW, CIPA CEO Rock Zierman noted energy companies were prepared to challenge the fresh ordinance.

Zierman added that it would make city residents more dependent on foreign oil from countries with lower environmental standards when they are "already struggling" with high gas prices.

"It sends the jobs, investment and revenue elsewhere while leaving Californians to pay the bill," said Zierman.

Recent findings suggest that the relationship between local oil production and prices at the pump is not straightforward and is influenced by a number of factors, according to the California Energy Commission, the state's main energy policy agency. Those include the cost of crude oil, refining, transportation, distribution and local taxes.

Industry observers note that even though the US is the world's largest oil producer, it exports and imports crude oil, as well as refined petroleum products. Because oil is traded globally, US residents are exposed to the same price fluctuations as people elsewhere, no matter how much of the fossil fuel is produced domestically.

Industry observers note that california's oil industry and the amount of oil it produces have been steadily declining since the 1980s. In the coastal lowlands known as the LA Basin, output is 43% lower than eight years ago, with the amount of oil extracted falling more rapidly than the number of open wells.

When wells stop producing, it is up to the oil operators to remove equipment and plug them. The state agency that regulates oil and gas, CalGEM, and the LA fire department oversee plugging operations, and also seal wells for which no-one takes responsibility.

But many have not yet been plugged — some 80% of idle wells in LA have been inactive for more than eight years, and about a third for over a century.

In a recent development, the cost of plugging a well also varies widely, with estimates ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars. California law requires operators to submit plugging prepares or face annual fines that increase with the amount of time the well has been idle.

It has been revealed that but those fines aren't always paid. According to CalGEM's own data, the agency collected just $1 million out of $36 million (€32 million) in fines in 2025.

A report by Carbon Tracker also found that if all future profits from oil companies operating in California went to decommissioning wells, the state would still face a shortfall of $7 billion. The cost would by default fall to taxpayers, according to Carbon Tracker.

Miranda told DW that the next step for community activists is to reduce the 20-year timeline and have the oil sector "pay for this cleanup."  For now, she is says both she and her mother are hopeful that future generations "can have better health and breathe cleaner air.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 13:45.

Liverpool are unlikely to give any consideration to a new contract for Alexis Mac Allister before February, Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The Argentina international is in the last two years of his current contract with Liverpool, having not signed a single extension since joining from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2023.

Mac Allister revealed in September that Liverpool were not in a position to offer him a upcoming contract, after the 27-year-old experienced a noticeable decline in individual performance levels in 2025-26.

However, after a positive World Cup with Argentina, Mac Allister has returned to form for Liverpool, scoring five goals and providing one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions so far this season.

The midfielder has started nine of Liverpool's 11 Premier League games under Andoni Iraola and also performed well in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United, creating two chances, completing 89% of his passes and winning four of his five ground duels.

Nevertheless, ex-Liverpool midfielder Hamann does not believe that talks over a upcoming deal will begin for another three months, and any extension is only likely to be two years at best.

"They remarked to him there's no contract now, and he's in his late 20s," Hamann told Sports Mole when asked if Mac Allister had already played his way into a new contract.

"If he carries on performing, if he keeps on scoring goals, then come February, March, April, there might be a time where you say. 'maybe we keep him another two years.' But I don't think there's any rush at the moment.".

Mac Allister - who turns 28 on December 24 - has come up with 24 goals and 21 assists in 167 matches for Liverpool since 2023, and he earns £180,000 a week under his current contract terms, according to Capology.

The Argentine's reported salary only makes him the 11th highest-paid player at Liverpool, below latest signing Ronald Araujo (£210k) and almost half of what Virgil van Dijk earns (£350k).

Mac Allister's relationship with Ryan Gravenberch blossomed to the maximum in the 2024-25 season, culminating in both midfielders becoming Premier League champions for the first time.

However, Mac Allister's decline from a defensive and box-to-box standpoint was striking; compared to 2024-25, he made 45% fewer tackles and 26% fewer recoveries than in the 2025-26 campaign.

Gravenberch's own form did not help the South American's cause, though, and the latter has had a rejuvenated look about him since the World Cup, immediately earning Iraola's trust in the process.

Mac Allister's availability remains exceptional too, as he has only missed 11 matches for club and country since joining Liverpool and has been involved in every match so far this season.

With Wataru Endo almost certainly on the way out and James McConnell still on the fringes, Liverpool should speed up the process of tying down Mac Allister, lest they risk losing another midfield option in 2027.

Didi Hamann was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of Lottoland Live Casino.

Interlull musings and shiny distractions

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on.
  • This time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally.
  • It has been revealed that any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on. The senior fixtures don’t start until Thursday, so we haven’t even got a fresh batch of international press conference quotes to sink our teeth into. Slim pickings.

This time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally. All the more so when you consider Noni Madueke can count himself unlucky to have missed out for England, while Bukayo Saka and William Saliba would ordinarily be shoo-ins.

It has been revealed that any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2. More minutes in his legs, rather than another injury to worry about.

Bolstered by Saliba and Max Dowman, whose domestic suspension kept him out of Saturday’s game, the youngsters ran out 5-2 winners. Given they’re currently 21st out of 31 teams in their Swiss-style league table, perhaps this is the way forward. Send the major guns down a level and start battering our way towards more club silverware. Relentless madman Arteta, finding fresh frontiers for his evil genius. He doesn’t just leave his technical area. He thinks outside it.

If you missed it, Max has been promoted to England’s under-21s for this window. He’ll join Arsenal loanees Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, as well as former Hale Enders Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who came off the bench for Hull on Saturday, and Amario Cozier-Duberry, who seems to be doing well at Middlesbrough on loan from Brighton.

Given Max has been in and around Mikel Arteta’s first team for a couple of seasons now, it’s easy to take milestones like this for granted. But playing under-21 international football at 16 is another significant step, even for someone whose talent has made rapid progress seem almost routine.

It has been revealed that back in September, Lee Carsley described his eventual promotion as inevitable, while stressing that the timing had to be right. The point was to bring him into a squad where he could play and compete, rather than move him up simply because everyone expected it.

Carsley referenced Nwaneri when discussing the temptation to push exceptional youngsters through the age groups. His point was that the aim is a long senior career, not winning a race to the first cap. That seems sensible enough. Max doesn’t need every appearance to become an audition for the next level.

A couple of games against Portugal and France should be a useful challenge in their own right. Carsley and Arteta also know each other from their Everton days, which ought to help when discussing what he needs.

With England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland hosting Euro 2028, you can imagine that tournament already features somewhere in Max’s ambitions. There’s plenty of football between now and then, though. For the moment, let’s see how he gets on with this next step.

Sources indicate that elsewhere, most of our European internationals will be occupied with the Nations League, while the South American trio rack up the air miles again. Piero Hincapie heads home to Ecuador for friendlies against Costa Rica and Bolivia, while Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes face Japan and Singapore, both in Singapore.

Recent findings suggest that I appreciate Brazil’s options are more limited when European teams are tied up with UEFA fixtures, but their friendly schedule does sometimes feel like somebody has thrown a dart at a map. No doubt the commercial logic is compelling, but that doesn’t make you any less worried about tired hamstrings.

Anyway, fingers crossed they all come back with their limbs intact.

In a recent development, in other news, Italian publication Tuttosport has named Andrea Berta the winner of its Best Executive Award at this year’s Golden Boy Awards. The Arsenal sporting director collects the gong three transfer windows into his tenure, the latest of which ended with some fans calling for his head after the failed pursuits of Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez.

According to recent reports, either the bar is pretty low, he’s basking in the reflected glory of the team’s success, or it’s one of those shindigs where buying an inordinately expensive table guarantees you something shiny to take home. The cynic in me wasn’t exactly silenced by the news that Joan Laporta won Best President and Jorge Mendes Best Agent. In fact, I snorted when I read that. And lest we forget, Edu picked up a similar award from the same organisers in 2023….

Myles Lewis-Skelly was in contention for the actual Golden Boy award, which went to Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi. Hard to argue too much with that, given the 19-year-old was at the heart of Spain’s World Cup win.

Cubarsi also made the FIFPRO World 11. More pertinently for us, so did David Raya. Having finished second to compatriot Unai Simon in the Ballon d’Or’s Best Goalkeeper category, I imagine there’s some satisfaction in getting the nod from the people who actually play the game. More than 26,000 professionals from 75 countries cast their votes, which is a fairly substantial dressing room to win over.

Alessia Russo, who is in fine form even if Arsenal Women are not, also earned her third selection for the Women’s World 11.

According to recent reports, as you’ll have gathered from the snippiness above, I find it easy to be cynical about these things. There are so many awards now that you half expect to get one for finding your seat at the ceremony. Still, sometimes it’s nice to give people a pat on the back and recognise a job well done.

Industry observers note that on an entirely unrelated note, have you voted for us to win Best Fan Media at the upcoming FSA Awards? You’ve only got a week left. A prestigious honour, that one. 😉.

Right, I think that’s as much toothpaste as I can squeeze out of a slow news day. If anything else happens, we’ll have it covered on Arseblog News. Catch you next time.

💡 Key Takeaways
